themes_detail.label: Graffiti surge in Queens Village
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 5 in the past week compared to a 0.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 1,150% increase (z-score: 6.65)—signaling either a coordinated tagging campaign or deteriorating public property maintenance THIS WEEK.
evidence: 5 graffiti complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,150% spike)
Z-score of 6.65 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Spike emerged last week, suggesting recent escalation rather than chronic pattern
reporting_angles: Ground-truth verification: visit locations where complaints were filed to document scope and nature of graffiti (tags, gang markers, etc.)
Interview Parks Dept. and local sanitation on response time and whether removal crews have been deployed

themes_detail.label: Vehicle noise complaints double
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints jumped to 11 THIS WEEK versus a 4.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 126% increase (z-score: 3.02)—indicating either increased motorcycle/modified exhaust activity or residents increasingly reporting the problem.
evidence: 11 vehicle noise complaints this week vs. 4.9 weekly average (126% spike)
Z-score of 3.02 meets statistical significance threshold
Spike is recent and acute, not part of long-running trend
reporting_angles: Survey residents on specific locations and times where vehicle noise is worst; interview affected families about sleep/quality of life impact
Check with NYPD on enforcement activity and whether illegal modified exhaust is being targeted; compare to citywide vehicle noise trends

themes_detail.label: Animal welfare complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary animal conditions on private property jumped to 4 complaints THIS WEEK compared to a 0.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 433% increase (z-score: 3.92)—suggesting either a cluster of hoarding/neglect cases or new awareness of enforcement options.
evidence: 4 unsanitary animal complaints this week vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% spike)
Spike is extremely recent (this week only), not a multi-week trend
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Animal Care & Control to learn if there is a known hoarding situation, kennel operation, or animal neglect case under investigation in the district
Interview residents in affected areas about living conditions and whether complaints have been filed with city enforcement agencies

themes_detail.label: Non-emergency police calls rise 36%
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matter complaints increased to 13 last week compared to a 5.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 136% spike (z-score: 2.94)—reflecting either elevated crime/disturbance complaints or increased resident willingness to call NYPD.
evidence: 13 non-emergency police matter complaints last week vs. 5.5 weekly average (136% spike)
Z-score of 2.94 meets statistical significance threshold
Spike is recent (last week), suggesting emerging pattern rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Analyze the types of incidents reported (trespassing, disorderly conduct, etc.) via FOIL request to NYPD to understand what is driving the increase
Compare to NYPD crime statistics and Compstat data for the precinct to see if reported crimes align with spike in 311 calls

themes_detail.label: Street signs damaged 2.5x baseline
themes_detail.summary: Damaged street sign complaints jumped to 7 two weeks ago compared to a 2.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 154% increase (z-score: 2.72)—indicating either vehicular impact damage or maintenance backlog in the district.
evidence: 7 damaged street sign complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.8 weekly average (154% spike)
Spike occurred 2 weeks ago; unclear if trend is sustaining or has resolved
reporting_angles: Verify with DOT whether street signs have been replaced or remain damaged; assess if damage is due to accidents, vandalism, or weather
Check if spike correlates with traffic incidents or road construction activity in the district
